notes: Public API and normal UI input only, in owned isolated Xvfb/Rhino sessions. No pre-existing user session was targeted; owned processes exited or were cleaned up before subsequent runs.

The original four-case open-object timeout remains retained separately. A manual owned-dialog inspection identified the warning and allowed the first mesh case to complete; it was not counted among these 42 automated observations.

A preliminary automated XSendEvent attempt required manual recovery of one waiting dialog, then failed with BadWindow during Escape key-up. Its terminal failure is retained, not converted into a successful response or a rejection observation.

Focused XTest input after a nonblocking settling interval completed the full 42 cases. The final capture renamed the literal Escape input from cancel to escape to avoid assuming its effect. Geometry, API values, output points/attributes and selection exactly reproduced the earlier completed capture; changing labels, transient window IDs and history were excluded from that repeat comparison.

Yes and Escape continued all warned cases; No produced the ten unsuccessful completions. The twelve closed/unoriented-closed controls displayed no warning and received no answer, irrespective of the requested choice.

Full numeric observations are retained with only JSON whitespace/key formatting changed. Near-zero API volumes, enormous surface API centroids and negative-volume getter discrepancies are not normalized or replaced with command targets.

The generator reads no observed targets. The initial capture-only implementation rejected native confirmation inputs. Current native boundary replay is documented separately and does not change the existing 26 closed-command comparison scope.
No Rhino Undo/Redo, general open-surface integration policy or timing parity is claimed. Current native compatibility is limited to the separately reported matches, with all counterexamples retained.
